course.title: Food Safety and Hygiene
course.tagline: Handle, store and serve food safely, and pass a food hygiene check.

days.title: Why Food Safety Matters
days.goal: Know why food safety matters and what can go wrong.

video.title: ServSafe Food Handler Test Pre exam — full Q&A walkthrough

steps: Unsafe food can make people very sick.
Germs are tiny living things you cannot see. They grow fast in food.
Food poisoning means sickness from eating unsafe food.
Anyone who handles food must keep it safe.
Good food safety protects your customers and your name.
days.task: Write down three reasons food safety matters.
days.challenge: List three foods that go bad fast.

quiz.q: What is food poisoning?
quiz.explain: Food poisoning is sickness caused by eating unsafe food.

quiz.q: What are germs?
options: Tiny living things you cannot see that grow fast in food
quiz.explain: Germs are tiny living things. You cannot see them, but they can make people sick.

quiz.q: Who must keep food safe?
quiz.explain: Everyone who touches food must keep it safe.

days.title: Handwashing: The First Rule
days.goal: Wash your hands the right way, every time.

video.title: Food Safety & Hygiene Training Video in English Level 1

steps: Wet your hands with clean water.
Add soap. Rub your hands for 20 seconds.
Rub between fingers, under nails, and on the backs of hands.
Rinse well and dry with a clean towel or paper.
Wash hands before cooking, after touching raw meat, and after the toilet.
days.task: Practise washing your hands for a full 20 seconds.
days.challenge: Time yourself and check you rub everywhere.

quiz.q: How long should you wash your hands?
quiz.explain: Twenty seconds with soap removes most germs.

quiz.q: When must you wash your hands?
options: Before cooking, after raw meat, and after the toilet
quiz.explain: Wash before cooking, after raw meat, and after the toilet.

quiz.q: Why rub between fingers and under nails?
quiz.explain: Germs hide between fingers and under nails.

days.title: Personal Hygiene for Food Handlers
days.goal: Keep yourself clean when you handle food.

video.title: ServSafe Chapter 3: The Safe Food Handler

steps: Wear clean clothes and a hair cover when you cook.
Keep nails short and clean. Do not wear nail polish.
Do not cook if you are sick with a stomach bug or a bad cold.
Cover cuts with a clean plaster and a glove.
Do not touch food with bare hands if you have a cut.
days.task: Check your clothes, nails, and hair before cooking today.
days.challenge: Write a personal hygiene checklist for your kitchen.

quiz.q: Why wear a hair cover?
options: So hair does not fall into food
quiz.explain: Hair in food is unhygienic and upsets customers.

quiz.q: Why keep nails short?
quiz.explain: Germs hide under long nails and can get into food.

quiz.q: Why not cook when you are sick?
options: You can pass germs to the food and make people sick
quiz.explain: A sick cook can pass germs into food.

days.title: The Danger Zone: Temperatures That Matter
days.goal: Learn the danger zone and keep food out of it.

video.title: Food Handler Safety Training

steps: The danger zone is 5°C to 60°C. Germs grow fast in this range.
Keep cold food below 5°C. Keep hot food above 60°C.
Do not leave food in the danger zone for more than 2 hours.
Use a food thermometer to check temperatures.
Write down fridge temperatures every day.
days.task: Check your fridge temperature with a thermometer.
days.challenge: Leave a plate of food out for 2 hours and throw it away. Note the rule.

quiz.q: What is the danger zone?
quiz.explain: The danger zone is 5°C to 60°C. Germs grow fast there.

quiz.q: How long can food sit in the danger zone?
quiz.explain: Food left out over 2 hours is not safe to eat.

quiz.q: What temperature must cold food stay below?
quiz.explain: Cold food must stay below 5°C.

days.title: Cooking Temperatures: Kill the Germs
days.goal: Cook food to safe temperatures.

video.title: Food Safety Modernization Act: Handwashing

steps: Chicken and turkey must reach 75°C inside.
Minced meat must reach 75°C inside.
Steaks and chops must reach 63°C, then rest for 3 minutes.
Fish must reach 63°C and flake easily.
Use a thermometer. Do not guess.
days.task: Cook chicken and check it reaches 75°C inside.
days.challenge: Cook a steak and check the temperature.

quiz.q: What temperature must chicken reach?
quiz.explain: Chicken must reach 75°C inside to kill germs.

quiz.q: Why use a thermometer?
options: You cannot see germs, so you must measure the heat
quiz.explain: A thermometer tells you the true inside temperature.

quiz.q: What temperature must minced meat reach?
quiz.explain: Minced meat must reach 75°C inside.

days.title: Cross-Contamination: Keep It Apart
days.goal: Stop germs moving from one food to another.

video.title: What is HACCP? | Food Safety Risks & Hazards

steps: Cross-contamination means germs move from one food to another.
Keep raw meat away from cooked food and ready-to-eat food.
Use different chopping boards for raw meat and vegetables.
Wash hands after touching raw meat.
Clean knives and boards between foods.
days.task: Set up two chopping boards: one for raw meat, one for vegetables.
days.challenge: Practise washing your hands and tools between foods.

quiz.q: What is cross-contamination?
options: Germs moving from one food to another
quiz.explain: Cross-contamination is germs moving from raw food to cooked or ready-to-eat food.

quiz.q: Why use different chopping boards?
options: So raw meat germs do not get onto vegetables
quiz.explain: Separate boards stop germs moving from raw meat to other food.

quiz.q: Why wash hands after raw meat?
options: To stop germs spreading to other food
quiz.explain: Raw meat has germs. Washing stops them spreading.

days.title: Week 1 Project: A Kitchen Safety Check
days.goal: Do a full food safety check of your kitchen.

video.title: Temperature Danger Zone Explained

steps: Check handwashing: soap, clean water, and towels.
Check fridge temperature: below 5°C.
Check storage: raw meat below cooked food.
Check boards and knives: separate ones for raw meat.
Check cleaning: surfaces clean, no old food lying around.
days.task: Do a full safety check of your kitchen and fix three problems.
days.challenge: Write a safety checklist for your kitchen.

quiz.q: What temperature must a fridge be?
quiz.explain: A fridge must be below 5°C to keep food safe.

quiz.q: Where should raw meat go in the fridge?
options: On the bottom shelf, below cooked food
quiz.explain: Raw meat goes on the bottom shelf so juices cannot drip onto cooked food.

quiz.q: Why check your kitchen weekly?
quiz.explain: Regular checks catch problems before they make people sick.

project.title: Do a Kitchen Safety Check
project.brief: Check handwashing, fridge, storage, boards, and cleaning in your kitchen.
checks: Handwashing checked: soap, water, towels
Fridge temperature below 5°C
Raw meat stored below cooked food
Separate boards for raw meat and vegetables
Surfaces clean, no old food lying around
Three problems found and fixed

days.title: Storing Food: Fridge and Freezer
days.goal: Store food safely in the fridge and freezer.

video.title: Food safety and storage

steps: Fridge: below 5°C. Freezer: below -18°C.
Store raw meat on the bottom shelf in sealed containers.
Store cooked food above raw meat.
Cover all food. Do not leave it open.
Label food with the date it was made or opened.
days.task: Organise your fridge: raw meat at the bottom, cooked food above.
days.challenge: Label three items in your fridge with dates.

quiz.q: What temperature must a freezer be?
quiz.explain: A freezer must be below -18°C to keep food frozen hard.

quiz.q: Why store raw meat on the bottom shelf?
options: So juices cannot drip onto cooked food
quiz.explain: Juices from raw meat can drip and spread germs.

quiz.q: Why label food with a date?
options: So you know when it was made and when to use it by
quiz.explain: A date tells you if food is still safe to eat.

days.title: Thawing Food Safely
days.goal: Thaw frozen food the safe way.

video.title: Learn Safe Food Handling | Professional Food Handler Full Course (FREE)

steps: Thaw in the fridge overnight. This is the safest way.
Thaw in cold water, changing the water every 30 minutes.
Thaw in the microwave, then cook at once.
Never thaw food on the counter at room temperature.
Do not refreeze food that has thawed.
days.task: Thaw frozen meat in the fridge overnight.
days.challenge: Thaw a small item in cold water and time it.

quiz.q: What is the safest way to thaw food?
quiz.explain: Thawing in the fridge keeps food cold and safe.

quiz.q: Why not thaw on the counter?
options: The outside warms into the danger zone while the inside is still frozen
quiz.explain: On the counter, the outside reaches the danger zone while the middle is still frozen.

quiz.q: Why not refreeze thawed food?
options: Germs grow while it thaws, so refreezing is not safe
quiz.explain: Germs grow during thawing. Refreezing does not kill them.

days.title: Cooling and Reheating Food
days.goal: Cool and reheat food safely.

video.title: Food Safety Training Manuals and Video One: Understanding the Importance of Food Safety and Roles We Play

steps: Cool cooked food fast: within 2 hours.
Put hot food in shallow containers so it cools fast.
Do not put very hot food in the fridge. Let steam stop first.
Reheat food until it is steaming hot all the way through, 75°C.
Reheat food only once. Throw away what is left.
days.task: Cool a pot of stew fast in shallow containers.
days.challenge: Reheat a portion and check it reaches 75°C.

quiz.q: How fast must cooked food cool?
quiz.explain: Food must cool within 2 hours to stay safe.

quiz.q: Why use shallow containers to cool food?
quiz.explain: Shallow containers let heat escape fast.

quiz.q: What temperature must reheated food reach?
quiz.explain: Reheated food must reach 75°C all the way through.

days.title: Cleaning and Sanitising
days.goal: Clean and sanitise your kitchen properly.

video.title: Basic Food Hygiene Certification Course

steps: Cleaning removes dirt. Sanitising kills germs.
Clean surfaces with soap and water first.
Then sanitise with a food-safe sanitiser or hot water.
Clean chopping boards and knives after each use.
Keep cleaning cloths clean. Wash them often.
days.task: Clean and sanitise your kitchen surfaces today.
days.challenge: Wash all your cleaning cloths.

quiz.q: What is the difference between cleaning and sanitising?
options: Cleaning removes dirt. Sanitising kills germs
quiz.explain: Cleaning removes dirt. Sanitising kills germs.

quiz.q: Why clean before you sanitise?
quiz.explain: Dirt blocks sanitiser. Clean first, then sanitise.

quiz.q: Why wash cleaning cloths often?
quiz.explain: A dirty cloth spreads germs instead of removing them.

days.title: Allergens: The 14 to Know
days.goal: Learn about food allergens and how to handle them.

video.title: Food Hygiene & HACCP Level 1 | Free Course

steps: An allergen is a food that can cause a bad reaction in some people.
Common allergens: peanuts, milk, eggs, fish, wheat, soy, and nuts.
Ask customers about allergies before you serve them.
Cook allergy-free food separately with clean tools.
Label dishes clearly so customers know what is in them.
days.task: Write a list of the 14 main allergens.
days.challenge: Practise cooking one dish separately with clean tools.

quiz.q: What is an allergen?
options: A food that can cause a bad reaction in some people
quiz.explain: An allergen is a food that triggers a bad reaction in some people.

quiz.q: What are common allergens?
options: Peanuts, milk, eggs, fish, wheat, soy, and nuts
quiz.explain: Peanuts, milk, eggs, fish, wheat, soy, and nuts are common allergens.

quiz.q: Why cook allergy-free food separately?
options: So allergens do not get into safe food
quiz.explain: Separate cooking with clean tools stops allergens getting into safe food.

days.title: HACCP: The Safety System
days.goal: Learn HACCP, the food safety system.

video.title: ServSafe Food Handler Test Pre exam — full Q&A walkthrough

steps: HACCP means Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points.
It is a system that finds dangers in food and controls them.
A critical control point is a step where you must control a danger, like cooking temperature.
Write down your critical points: cooking, cooling, and storage.
Check them every day and write the results down.
days.task: Write down three critical control points in your kitchen.
days.challenge: Check one point today and write the result down.

quiz.q: What does HACCP stand for?
options: Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points
quiz.explain: HACCP stands for Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points.

quiz.q: What is a critical control point?
options: A step where you must control a danger, like cooking temperature
quiz.explain: A critical control point is a step where a danger must be controlled.

quiz.q: Why write results down?
options: So you can prove food was kept safe
quiz.explain: Written records prove you controlled the dangers.

days.title: Week 2 Project: A Food Safety Audit
days.goal: Audit a kitchen for food safety.

video.title: Food Safety & Hygiene Training Video in English Level 1

steps: Check handwashing, personal hygiene, and clothing.
Check temperatures: fridge, freezer, and cooking.
Check storage: raw and cooked food apart, labels on everything.
Check cleaning: surfaces, boards, knives, and cloths.
Write a report with problems found and fixes.
days.task: Audit your kitchen and write a report.
days.challenge: Fix the three biggest problems you found.

quiz.q: What is a food safety audit?
options: A full check of a kitchen for food safety
quiz.explain: An audit is a full check of a kitchen for food safety.

quiz.q: What should an audit check?
quiz.explain: An audit checks hygiene, temperatures, storage, and cleaning.

quiz.q: Why write a report?
options: So problems are recorded and fixed
quiz.explain: A written report makes sure problems get fixed.

project.title: Audit a Kitchen for Food Safety
project.brief: Do a full food safety audit and write a report.
checks: Handwashing and hygiene checked
Fridge, freezer, and cooking temperatures checked
Storage checked: raw and cooked apart, labels on
Cleaning checked: surfaces, boards, knives, cloths
Report written with problems and fixes
Three biggest problems fixed

days.title: Foodborne Illness: Germs That Make People Sick
days.goal: Learn the germs that cause food poisoning.

video.title: ServSafe Chapter 3: The Safe Food Handler

steps: Salmonella lives in raw chicken and eggs.
E. coli lives in raw minced meat.
Listeria grows in cold food like soft cheese and deli meat.
Cooking food well kills most germs.
Washing hands and keeping food cold stops germs growing.
days.task: Write a list of three germs and where they live.
days.challenge: List three ways to stop germs growing.

quiz.q: Where does Salmonella live?
quiz.explain: Salmonella lives in raw chicken and eggs.

quiz.q: How do you kill most germs in food?
options: Cooking it to a safe temperature
quiz.explain: Cooking to a safe temperature kills most germs.

quiz.q: How do you stop germs growing?
options: Washing hands and keeping food cold
quiz.explain: Handwashing and cold storage stop germs growing.

days.title: Receiving Deliveries Safely
days.goal: Check food deliveries when they arrive.

video.title: Food Handler Safety Training

steps: Check the temperature of cold deliveries. They must be cold.
Check dates: do not accept food past its use-by date.
Check packaging: do not accept torn or dirty packs.
Store deliveries at once. Do not leave them out.
Write down what arrived and when.
days.task: Practise checking a delivery at home.
days.challenge: Write a delivery checklist.

quiz.q: What should you check first on a delivery?
quiz.explain: Check temperature, dates, and packaging first.

quiz.q: Why not accept food past its use-by date?
options: It may not be safe to eat
quiz.explain: Food past its use-by date may not be safe.

quiz.q: Why store deliveries at once?
options: So food does not sit in the danger zone
quiz.explain: Leaving deliveries out lets food warm into the danger zone.

days.title: Pest Control: Keep Pests Out
days.goal: Keep pests out of your kitchen.

video.title: Food Safety Modernization Act: Handwashing

steps: Pests are rats, mice, cockroaches, and flies.
Keep food in sealed containers.
Clean up spills and crumbs at once.
Take rubbish out often and keep bins closed.
Seal gaps in walls and doors.
days.task: Check your kitchen for gaps and open food.
days.challenge: Clean your kitchen and take out the rubbish.

quiz.q: What are pests in a kitchen?
quiz.explain: Pests are rats, mice, cockroaches, and flies.

quiz.q: Why keep food in sealed containers?
quiz.explain: Sealed containers keep pests out of food.

quiz.q: Why clean spills at once?
quiz.explain: Spills and crumbs attract pests.

days.title: Waste and Rubbish: Handle It Safely
days.goal: Handle kitchen waste safely.

video.title: What is HACCP? | Food Safety Risks & Hazards

steps: Put waste in bins with lids.
Take rubbish out often. Do not let it pile up.
Wash bins often.
Wash your hands after handling rubbish.
Keep waste away from food preparation areas.
days.task: Clean your bins today.
days.challenge: Set up a waste routine for your kitchen.

quiz.q: Why use bins with lids?
options: Lids keep pests out and stop smells
quiz.explain: Lids keep pests out and stop smells spreading.

quiz.q: Why wash hands after rubbish?
quiz.explain: Rubbish carries germs. Washing stops them spreading to food.

quiz.q: Why keep waste away from food areas?
options: Waste can spread germs to food
quiz.explain: Waste near food can spread germs.

days.title: Food Safety at Events and Catering
days.goal: Keep food safe at events.

video.title: Temperature Danger Zone Explained

steps: Keep hot food hot and cold food cold during transport.
Use coolers and chafing dishes at events.
Do not leave food out for more than 2 hours.
Serve with clean utensils. Do not let guests touch food with hands.
Label dishes, especially those with allergens.
days.task: Pack food for an event using coolers.
days.challenge: Set up a serving table with labels.

quiz.q: How do you keep food safe during transport?
options: Use coolers to keep hot food hot and cold food cold
quiz.explain: Coolers hold food at safe temperatures during transport.

quiz.q: How long can food sit out at an event?
quiz.explain: Food left out over 2 hours is not safe.

quiz.q: Why label dishes at events?
options: So guests with allergies know what is safe
quiz.explain: Labels help guests with allergies choose safe food.

days.title: Food Safety Mistakes and Fixes
days.goal: Fix the commonest food safety mistakes.

video.title: Food safety and storage

steps: Forgot to wash hands? Wash now and do not touch food until you do.
Left food out too long? Throw it away. Do not taste it to check.
Used the same board for meat and vegetables? Wash it and start again.
Fridge too warm? Check the setting and call for repair if needed.
Write down each mistake and fix.
days.task: Fix one food safety mistake you have made.
days.challenge: Write a list of three mistakes and how you would fix them.

quiz.q: What do you do with food left out too long?
quiz.explain: Food left out too long is not safe. Throw it away.

quiz.q: What do you do if you used the same board for meat and vegetables?
options: Wash it well and start again
quiz.explain: Wash the board well to remove germs before using it again.

quiz.q: Why not taste food to check if it is safe?
quiz.explain: Germs have no taste. Tasting cannot tell you if food is safe.

days.title: Week 3 Project: Pass a Hygiene Check
days.goal: Prepare for and pass a food hygiene check.

video.title: Learn Safe Food Handling | Professional Food Handler Full Course (FREE)

steps: Do a full audit of your kitchen.
Fix every problem you find.
Write down your temperatures, cleaning, and storage rules.
Train a friend or family member on the rules.
Invite someone to check your kitchen and give you a score.
days.task: Do a full hygiene check of your kitchen.
days.challenge: Ask someone to score your kitchen and note what to improve.

quiz.q: What is a hygiene check?
options: A check that your kitchen follows food safety rules
quiz.explain: A hygiene check tests if your kitchen follows food safety rules.

quiz.q: Why write your rules down?
options: So everyone follows the same rules
quiz.explain: Written rules help everyone do the right thing.

quiz.q: Why train others on the rules?
options: So the whole kitchen stays safe
quiz.explain: Everyone in the kitchen must know the rules.

project.title: Pass a Food Hygiene Check
project.brief: Prepare your kitchen and pass a hygiene check by a friend.
checks: Full audit done
All problems found and fixed
Temperatures, cleaning, and storage rules written
Someone trained on the rules
Kitchen checked by someone else
Score received and improvements noted

days.title: Food Labels: Dates and Meanings
days.goal: Read food labels and dates correctly.

video.title: Food Safety Training Manuals and Video One: Understanding the Importance of Food Safety and Roles We Play

steps: Use-by date: do not eat food after this date. It may not be safe.
Best-before date: food may still be safe after this date, but quality drops.
Check ingredients for allergens.
Check storage instructions: fridge, freezer, or cupboard.
Throw away food past its use-by date.
days.task: Check five items in your kitchen for dates.
days.challenge: Throw away anything past its use-by date.

quiz.q: What does use-by mean?
options: Do not eat after this date. It may not be safe
quiz.explain: Use-by is about safety. Do not eat food after this date.

quiz.q: What does best-before mean?
options: Do not eat after this date
Food may still be safe, but quality drops
quiz.explain: Best-before is about quality, not safety.

quiz.q: Why check storage instructions?
options: So you store food the right way
quiz.explain: Storage instructions tell you where food stays safe.

days.title: Safe Food for Babies and Old People
days.goal: Take extra care with food for babies and old people.

video.title: Basic Food Hygiene Certification Course

steps: Babies and old people get sick more easily from unsafe food.
Cook their food well. Do not serve raw or undercooked food.
Use fresh ingredients and clean tools.
Serve food at the right temperature, not too hot.
Ask about allergies and diets.
days.task: Cook a meal for a baby or an older person with extra care.
days.challenge: Write a checklist for cooking for vulnerable people.

quiz.q: Why take extra care with food for babies?
options: They get sick more easily from unsafe food
quiz.explain: Babies and old people are more at risk from food poisoning.

quiz.q: What food should you avoid for babies?
quiz.explain: Raw or undercooked food can carry germs that harm babies.

quiz.q: Why ask about diets for old people?
options: So you cook food that suits them
quiz.explain: Old people may have diets or allergies you must respect.

days.title: Your Food Safety Plan
days.goal: Write your own food safety plan.

video.title: Food Hygiene & HACCP Level 1 | Free Course

steps: List your rules: handwashing, temperatures, storage, and cleaning.
List your critical control points: cooking, cooling, and storage.
Write who does what in your kitchen.
Write how often you check each point.
Keep the plan where everyone can see it.
days.task: Write your food safety plan.
days.challenge: Show it to a friend and ask for feedback.

quiz.q: What is a food safety plan?
options: A written plan of your safety rules and checks
quiz.explain: A food safety plan writes down your rules and checks.

quiz.q: Why write who does what?
quiz.explain: Clear jobs mean nothing is missed.

quiz.q: Why keep the plan where everyone can see it?
quiz.explain: A visible plan reminds everyone of the rules.

days.title: Training Others in Food Safety
days.goal: Teach food safety to others.

video.title: ServSafe Food Handler Test Pre exam — full Q&A walkthrough

steps: Teach handwashing first. It is the most important rule.
Show, then let them try, then watch them do it alone.
Use simple words. No jargon.
Check their work kindly and give feedback.
Ask them to teach someone else.
days.task: Teach handwashing to a friend or family member.
days.challenge: Teach one more food safety rule to someone else.

quiz.q: What should you teach first?
quiz.explain: Handwashing is the most important food safety rule.

quiz.q: Why use simple words?
quiz.explain: Simple words help everyone learn.

quiz.q: Why ask them to teach someone else?
options: Teaching proves they really know it
quiz.explain: If they can teach it, they truly understand it.

days.title: Food Safety Certificates
days.goal: Learn about food safety certificates.

video.title: Food Safety & Hygiene Training Video in English Level 1

steps: A certificate shows you have learned food safety.
Many jobs ask for a food hygiene certificate.
You can take a course online or in person.
The course covers handwashing, temperatures, storage, and HACCP.
Keep your certificate safe. Show it when you apply for jobs.
days.task: Find a food hygiene course in your area or online.
days.challenge: List what the course covers.

quiz.q: What is a food hygiene certificate?
options: Proof you have learned food safety
quiz.explain: A certificate proves you have learned food safety.

quiz.q: Why do jobs ask for one?
options: So employers know you can handle food safely
quiz.explain: A certificate shows an employer you know food safety.

quiz.q: What does a food hygiene course cover?
quiz.explain: A food hygiene course covers the main safety rules.

days.title: Keeping Records: Temperatures and Checks
days.goal: Keep simple records of your food safety checks.

video.title: ServSafe Chapter 3: The Safe Food Handler

steps: Write down fridge and freezer temperatures every day.
Write down cooking temperatures for meat.
Write down cleaning times.
Keep all records in one book or file.
Show records to an inspector if they ask.
days.task: Start a food safety record book today.
days.challenge: Record your fridge temperature for a week.

quiz.q: Why write down temperatures?
options: So you can prove food was kept safe
quiz.explain: Written temperatures prove you kept food safe.

quiz.q: Why keep records in one place?
options: So you can find them fast
quiz.explain: One place for records makes checks easy.

quiz.q: Why show records to an inspector?
options: So they can see you follow the rules
quiz.explain: Records prove to an inspector that you follow food safety rules.

days.title: Food Safety in Your Business
days.goal: Use food safety to build trust in your business.

video.title: Food Handler Safety Training

steps: Tell customers you follow food safety rules.
Show your certificate if you have one.
Keep your kitchen clean and let customers see it.
Handle complaints about food safety seriously and fast.
Good food safety is good business.
days.task: Write a short note about food safety for your customers.
days.challenge: Show your kitchen to a customer and ask what they think.

quiz.q: Why tell customers about food safety?
quiz.explain: Customers trust businesses that care about food safety.

quiz.q: Why show your certificate?
options: It proves you know food safety
quiz.explain: A certificate proves your knowledge to customers.

quiz.q: Why handle food safety complaints fast?
quiz.explain: Food safety complaints can harm people. Handle them fast.

days.title: Revision: The Food Safety Skills Check
days.goal: Revisit the core skills of the course.

video.title: Food Safety Modernization Act: Handwashing

steps: Wash your hands the right way from memory.
Name the danger zone temperatures.
Explain cross-contamination in one sentence.
Name three allergens.
List your three strongest skills and one to improve.
days.task: Do a full kitchen safety check from memory, no notes.
days.challenge: Teach one food safety rule to a friend or family member.

quiz.q: What is the danger zone?
quiz.explain: The danger zone is 5°C to 60°C.

quiz.q: What is cross-contamination?
options: Germs moving from one food to another
quiz.explain: Cross-contamination is germs moving from one food to another.

quiz.q: Why teach a rule to someone else?
options: Teaching proves you really know it
quiz.explain: If you can teach it, you truly understand it.

days.title: Capstone Prep: Plan Your Final Safety Audit
days.goal: Plan your capstone food safety audit.

video.title: What is HACCP? | Food Safety Risks & Hazards

steps: Choose a kitchen to audit: yours or a friend's.
Write your audit checklist: hygiene, temperatures, storage, cleaning.
Plan how you will fix problems you find.
Check you have a thermometer and cleaning supplies.
Do a trial audit if you have time.
days.task: Write your complete capstone audit plan.
days.challenge: Do a trial audit of your kitchen today.

quiz.q: What should your capstone show?
options: Everything you learned: hygiene, temperatures, storage, cleaning, and HACCP
quiz.explain: The capstone proves the whole course.

quiz.q: Why plan how to fix problems?
options: So problems are fixed, not just found
quiz.explain: Finding problems is not enough. You must fix them.

quiz.q: Why do a trial audit?
options: To find problems before the real audit
quiz.explain: A trial audit finds problems while there is still time to fix them.

capstone.title: The Food Safety Audit: Check a Kitchen and Make It Safe
capstone.brief: Do a full food safety audit of a real kitchen: check handwashing, personal hygiene, temperatures, storage, thawing, cleaning, allergens, and HACCP points. Write a report, fix the problems you find, and train one person on the rules.
checks: Full audit done: hygiene, temperatures, storage, cleaning
Danger zone and cooking temperatures checked with a thermometer
Cross-contamination risks found and fixed
Allergen handling checked and labelled
HACCP points written down and checked
Report written with problems and fixes
One person trained on the food safety rules
deliverables: Your written audit report with problems and fixes
Your food safety plan written in your own words
Your temperature records for one week
A short note on what you learned and what you will improve next
